claims.text: The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs can be understood by analyzing correlations between electrical and magnetic properties.
Principles used to design magnetism in high-entropy oxides can explain ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
The initial material is a near-equiatomic HEA.
The HEA thin films can be fabricated by pulse electrodeposition in an aqueous medium.
The material is characterized at room temperature.
The magnetic properties are measured using vibrating sample magnetometry and ferromagnetic resonance.
The deposited HEA has a dual-phase FCC+BCC structure.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties influences the formation of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
Magnetism-design behavior in high-entropy oxides influences the formation of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
The fabricated HEA films will have a saturation magnetization of approximately 80 emu/g.
The fabricated HEA films will have a relatively low coercivity of approximately 20 Oe.
The HEA composition is uniform throughout the film.
The HEA film contains no distinct chemical phases.
The HEA grain size ranges from approximately 5 to 20 nm.
Saturation magnetization and coercivity can vary with composition and processing conditions.
A substantial deviation of saturation magnetization or coercivity from the predicted values, or observation of a different phase structure, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies two phases, FCC and BCC, whereas the baseline says that the film has no different chemical phases. Without clarifying that the baseline concerns compositional segregation rather than crystallographic phases, these statements conflict.
